name: Famous Paintings
description: The paintings everyone recognises and the artists behind them, from the Mona Lisa to The Starry Night and Guernica.

checkpoints.name: Cave walls to the Middle Ages
checkpoints.note: People paint animals on cave walls at Lascaux, and in China painters unroll scenes of city life along silk scrolls.

checkpoints.name: The Renaissance
checkpoints.note: Van Eyck in Flanders and Leonardo, Botticelli, Michelangelo and Raphael in Italy paint with perspective, oil and real light.

checkpoints.name: Baroque and the Dutch Golden Age
checkpoints.note: Caravaggio lights Rome's churches with sudden shadow, while Spanish kings and Dutch merchants hire painters who catch light, character and daily life, and put the viewer inside the picture.

checkpoints.name: Romanticism
checkpoints.note: Painters turn to politics, disaster and nature, while Japanese woodblock prints reach Europe and change how artists see.

checkpoints.name: Impressionism and after
checkpoints.note: Impressionists, Post-Impressionists and their followers paint light and feeling, and nervous or golden images become icons.

checkpoints.name: Modern art
checkpoints.note: Cubism, Surrealism, protest and Pop turn paintings into statements, Jackson Pollock lets paint drip across the canvas, and a painted soup can sits beside an old master in the museum.

checkpoints.name: Contemporary art
checkpoints.note: Art becomes a global market. Damien Hirst pickles a shark, Banksy paints walls and shreds his own picture at auction, Kusama's infinity rooms draw queues, and records keep breaking.
